newsitem.title: USA: California puts bond documents on Internet.
newsitem.headline: California puts bond documents on Internet.

text.p: California on Monday became the first state in the nation to use the Internet to offer complete documents detailing an upcoming bond sale, the state's treasurer said.
California state Treasurer Matt Fong said people will be able to access the preliminary official statement for a $525 million general obligation bond through his home page at www.treasurer.ca.gov.

"As technology changes, state government needs to adapt," Fong said. "It's fitting that we are on the cutting edge through this offering since California accounts for nearly a quarter of the nation's high-tech sales and jobs."

The documents available on-line detail a $525 million general obligation bond sale that will help to finance water reclamation, rail, higher education, libraries, new prisons, seismic retrofitting and other projects.
The competitive bond sale is tentatively set for March 18, but that date and the exact size of the deal could change based on market conditions, the treasurer's office said.
